title: How religions spread
examples: How did Christianity spread across the Roman Empire?

figure.label: Religions travelled along roads, seas and trade routes

explain.say: Religions travel with people. On this map, each line is a faith on the move, carried by traders, travelling teachers, rulers and families who moved to new lands.

Buddhism spread first with the Indian emperor Ashoka, who sent teachers to Sri Lanka and beyond. Then monks and merchants carried it along the Silk Road to China by around the first century, and on to Korea and Japan.

draw.label: Buddhism: by emperor, monk and merchant

draw.text: The monk Xuanzang walked from China to India in the 600s and brought back scriptures.

explain.say: Christianity spread from Jerusalem along Roman roads and sea lanes. Apostles such as Paul travelled the Mediterranean, and after Emperor Constantine allowed Christianity in 313, it grew across the empire, and later around the world.

draw.label: Christianity: along Roman roads and seas

explain.say: Islam spread quickly after the Prophet Muhammad's death in 632, as Muslim rulers' lands stretched from Spain to Central Asia. Later, traders and Sufi teachers carried it across the Indian Ocean to Indonesia and over the Sahara to West Africa.

draw.label: Islam: by rulers, then by traders and teachers

explain.say: So religions spread in four main ways: along trade routes, through teachers and missionaries, through rulers and empires, and through migration. Today the internet adds a fifth way.
Here is the story in order. Notice that spread was usually slow, over centuries, and that each faith took on new languages, art and customs wherever it settled.

items: 3rd century BCE: Ashoka sends Buddhist teachers
1st century CE: Paul travels the Mediterranean
7th to 8th century: Islam from Spain to Central Asia
13th century onward: Islam reaches Southeast Asia
20th century: migration carries every faith worldwide

faq.a: Buddhism reached China along the Silk Road, the trade routes linking India and Central Asia with China. Monks and merchants brought it by around the first century CE, and later Chinese pilgrims such as Xuanzang travelled to India and brought scriptures back to be translated.
asks: how did Buddhism get to China
when did Buddhism come to China

faq.a: Christianity spread from Jerusalem through Jesus's followers, the apostles, who travelled the Roman roads and the Mediterranean. After Emperor Constantine allowed it in 313 it grew quickly, and much later missionaries and European empires carried it to the Americas, Africa and Asia.
asks: how did Christianity become so big
how did Christianity spread across the world

faq.a: In the century after the Prophet Muhammad's death in 632, the lands ruled by Muslim caliphs stretched from Spain to Central Asia. In many other places, such as Indonesia and West Africa, Islam spread mainly through traders, scholars and Sufi teachers rather than armies.
asks: how did Islam become so big
how did Islam spread so fast

faq.a: Islam reached Indonesia and Malaysia mainly through Muslim traders and teachers sailing the Indian Ocean, from around the 1200s onward. Local rulers and their people gradually took up the faith, and today Indonesia has one of the largest Muslim populations in the world.
asks: why are there so many Muslims in Indonesia
how did Islam get to Southeast Asia

faq.a: Ashoka was an Indian emperor of the Maurya dynasty in the 3rd century BCE. After a bloody war he embraced Buddhism, carved messages about kindness on pillars and rocks, and sent Buddhist teachers to other lands, including Sri Lanka.
asks: what did Ashoka do for Buddhism

faq.a: A missionary is someone who travels to share their faith with other people, often also running schools or hospitals. Christianity, Buddhism and Islam have all had travelling teachers, though not every religion seeks new followers; Judaism and Hinduism, for example, generally do not send missionaries.

The Silk Road was a network of trade routes linking China, Central Asia, India, Persia and the Mediterranean. Along with silk and spices, it carried ideas, art and religions, including Buddhism, Christianity, Manichaeism and Islam.
asks: how did the Silk Road spread religion
what travelled on the Silk Road

faq.q: How did Hinduism spread outside India?
faq.a: Hindu ideas travelled with traders and priests to Southeast Asia long ago: the great temple of Angkor Wat in Cambodia was first built as a Hindu temple, and Bali in Indonesia is still mostly Hindu. In modern times migration has taken Hindu communities to Britain, North America, the Caribbean, Fiji and East Africa.

A diaspora is a community living far from its homeland while keeping its identity. The Jewish diaspora grew after the Romans destroyed the Temple in Jerusalem in the year 70, and today Sikh, Hindu, Muslim and many other communities live around the world through migration.

Buddhism reached Japan from Korea in the 500s CE, when a Korean kingdom sent Buddhist images and scriptures to the Japanese court. It then grew alongside Shinto, and many Japanese people take part in both traditions.
asks: when did Buddhism come to Japan
how did Buddhism get to Korea and Japan

faq.q: How did Sikhism spread around the world?
faq.a: Sikhism began in the Punjab, and it spread mainly through migration. In the 1900s many Sikhs moved to Britain, Canada, the United States, East Africa and elsewhere, building gurdwaras wherever they settled.
asks: why are there Sikhs in Canada
how did Sikhs come to Britain

faq.q: Do religions change when they spread?
faq.a: Yes, often. A faith usually keeps its core beliefs but takes on local languages, art, food and customs. Buddhism in Tibet, Thailand and Japan looks quite different, and Christian and Muslim festivals are celebrated in many local styles.
asks: why does Buddhism look different in different countries
do religions adapt to new cultures

faq.q: Were religions ever spread by force?
faq.a: Sometimes, yes. History includes forced conversions and wars connected with religion, and many faiths have been both spreaders and victims. Historians also stress that most lasting spread came slowly, through trade, teaching, marriage and migration, and that it differed greatly from place to place.

facts: Emperor Ashoka, in the 3rd century BCE, sent Buddhist teachers from India to Sri Lanka and other lands.
Buddhism reached China along the Silk Road by around the first century CE.
Emperor Constantine allowed Christians to worship freely in 313 CE, with the Edict of Milan.
Islam reached Indonesia mainly through Indian Ocean traders and teachers from around the 13th century.
Angkor Wat in Cambodia was first built as a Hindu temple in the 12th century and later became Buddhist.
